title: How Claude is winning business in enterprise companies
description: How Claude is winning business in enterprise companies
transcript: If you want to understand why Claude is winning the AI race when it comes to enterprise and business, we need to take a step back because Anthropic figured out something that most AI companies missed. And that is not to just build the best AI model or agent. It's actually to learn how companies work. Because here's the real problem, a lot of businesses don't know how to implement AI. But here are three clever strategies they're using to build that pathway to connect the two dots. First up, we have free education. They have courses for literally anybody at any level for small business. And quite honestly, it's very simple to understand. And I absolutely love the design that they have here. It's not boring and corporate. Number two, they're deploying Anthropic AI engineers to work directly with their customers so that Anthropic isn't guessing what the next feature should be. They're learning every little thing about the business from the inside. So from here, it understands every business has different processes. But how do we scale this out to everybody? They need a distribution layer. So they invest $100 million into the Claude partner program. Partners like Blackstone, Hellman & Friedman, and Goldman Sachs, where they provide direct training for these consultants so they can go out to other enterprise companies and implement AI and change management. For example, with PwC, they haven't only identified where the biggest gains are, they actually cross-pollinated between each other. So in this example with the office of CFO, they paired PwC's finance expertise with Anthropic's product set. So Claude co-work, Claude code. Essentially making PwC the customer zero. And in reverse, PwC helped Anthropic with their CFO operations. So that way, both companies understand from their domain expertise on how to implement AI to their own clients. Now that Anthropic has been deeply rooted into a lot of enterprise companies, have they actually won and how long are they going to stay there for? Let me know in the comments.
